text: From the independent review of #918 before it merged, on how P-0881 is carried out. One size larger, a conformance check that TLC ends because it can't read what the run recorded is invalid execution evidence and fails, as it does at the ratified bounds. The build had recorded every check TLC ended as failed as an operational end, which claims nothing under D-0070, so a run that recorded a start of -1 against a model over the naturals, or a step to a boolean or to 2**40, passed. The gate tells the two apart by what TLC and its runner report, and never by words a recorded value could put in a message. TLC's own exit status for a module it can't parse (150), or for a step or an invariant it can't evaluate (75, 76), fails the check, and so does its general status (255) when its message is the one for a number past its integers. A check that carries the runner's own error, a result with no TLC version (a stall, memory, a kill) and any other status still claim nothing. A check TLC ended this way stands whatever became of another check, as a completed count disagreement does, and the every-step check is held to the same rule. When the shared allowance has run out, nothing is claimed, as before. Left as it was: TLC's other general errors stay operational, so evidence that ends TLC some other way claims nothing one size larger. Receipts say a larger failure once, by invocation, and a receipt without components gives the gate's words in its row when the counts agree.
